selected_problem: Fresh-main inspection after v0.12.84 found that Base64 canonicality and byte/hash self-consistency were enforced only when apply/rollback consumed a changeset. ChangesetStore.get still returned durable before/after images whose Base64, size or SHA-256 disagreed with the persisted bytes, allowing ordinary readers to consume a changeset that the side-effect path would later reject as corrupt.
decision_basis: The repository already treats get() as the shared protocol/shape read boundary, so extending the same read boundary with the already-existing stagedBeforeBytes/stagedAfterBytes invariants is parity rather than a new storage architecture.
No new integrity algorithm or trust model is introduced; the repair reuses the existing canonical Base64, byte-count and SHA-256 checks.
The defect is directly falsifiable by modifying only persisted image metadata while leaving the public shape valid.
changes: core/changesets.mjs adds verifiedDurableChangeset(), which runs the existing protocol/shape verifier and then validates every persisted before/after image before get() returns it.
ChangesetStore.get now fails closed on image corruption rather than exposing a structurally valid but semantically corrupt durable changeset.
tests/changeset-read-image-integrity.test.mjs adds corrupted postimage, corrupted preimage and intact-read regressions.

verification.pre_fix_observation: PASS: fresh main get() invoked only verifiedChangesetProtocol(), while stagedBeforeBytes/stagedAfterBytes were deferred to apply/rollback.
verification.bounded_image_replay: 3/3 PASS: postimage hash mutation rejected; preimage size mutation rejected; intact before/after images accepted using the exact existing decode/size/SHA-256 predicates.
verification.regression_test_added: tests/changeset-read-image-integrity.test.mjs exercises the real ChangesetStore.get boundary for both image directions.
verification.hosted_runtime: Developer Execution Runtime remains transiently unavailable with HTTP 502; no hosted DWAC execution success is claimed.

truth_boundary: This cycle validates durable image self-consistency on read. Independent provenance/authentication, full durable resource-budget revalidation and stronger temporal semantics remain separate boundaries.
